Subject: Finova decision criteria: latency / cost / SLA - follow-up

Thanks again for the call today, Alyssa 1 appreciate you and Tom walking through the priority use-cases. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can align the next steps and get the internal teams looped in.

Recap (from our notes):
- Primary early use-case: customer support triage + automated summary for human agents (short chat flows, ~<=256 tokens typical).
- Data sensitivity: contains customer PII; security and data residency are requirements for production.
- Evaluation ask: pilot with representative traffic, followed by decision for production deployment (preferred private VPC or dedicated pool).

Clarifying questions / info we need to finalize decision criteria:
1) Latency targets: can you confirm p50 and p95 targets for the production flows? (We remember you mentioning ~300ms p50 in the call, but wanted to confirm).
2) Cost targets: is there an explicit cost-per-1k-token target or budget we should be aware of for production?
3) Deployment mode preference: pilot vs production 1 which mode do you expect to select (Hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, or Private/VPC/on-prem)?
4) Procurement/legal: who is the economic buyer and what is your typical procurement timeline (PO, SOW, security review windows)?

Next steps we propose:
- If you can confirm the bullets above, we’ll draft (a) a short perf test plan, (b) SLA & contract draft for procurement, and (c) a security evidence bundle (SOC2 + architecture note).
- Offer to run a short perf run with a small dedicated pool against a representative prompt set (we’ll need sample prompts / traffic profile).
- Suggest 30-min follow-up next Wednesday to review numbers and align on procurement timeline.

Thanks 1 copying Marissa to lead technical onboarding and Rishi to scope the perf run.

Regards,
Marcus Lin

Thanks Marcus 1 nice summary. Confirming details from our side and adding stakeholders:

Stakeholders / economic buyer:
- Tom Benson (CTO) 1 economic buyer and final approver for infra spend.
- Sarah Liu (Head of Security) 1 will lead security/compliance review.
- Janet Morris (Procurement) 1 handles SOW/PO and contract routing.

Decision criteria were prioritizing:
- Latency: target p50 <= 300ms, p95 <= 800ms for short chat flows (~<=256 tokens). For longer generation flows we can accept higher tail latencies but want clear SLOs.
- Cost: were aiming for a production cost profile that keeps incremental inference spend under ~$0.10 per 1k tokens equivalent for the initial volume tier (we’re still modeling volume).
- Deployment: preference for Private (VPC) for production due to data residency and logging requirements; open to Dedicated for pilot to speed time-to-value.
- SLA: would like 99.9% availability target with clear credit/response terms for incidents and RTOs 1 Sarah will provide exact legal language once she’s had a first pass.

Procurement timeline:
- Security review (Sarah): ~2–3 weeks for initial questionnaire review, may require evidence (SOC2, architecture diagram, data retention details).
- Procurement (Janet): procurement + legal review typically 3–4 weeks after security sign-off. PO issuance expected in May if everything aligns.

I’m attaching our security questionnaire for your info 1 Sarah will follow up with more specifics if needed.

Happy to schedule the follow-up 1 Tom’s calendar is tight next week but Wed morning PT looks feasible.

Best,
Alyssa

alyssa@finova.com

Perfect 1 thanks for the clarity, Alyssa. Helpful to have the stakeholder list and initial targets. A few quick datapoints from similar pilots and proposed next steps: 

Latency: for short chat flows (<=256 tokens) we typically see on Dedicated pools: p50 in the ~120–220ms range and p95 in the ~450–700ms range depending on model size and batching. Private/VPC deployments typically match Dedicated performance if the same instance types and configs are used.

Cost: ballpark (order-of-magnitude) cost delta: Hosted API (managed) tends to be higher per-token vs Dedicated vs Private. We can provide a tighter estimate once we see representative traffic; for planning we’ll model both Dedicated reserved and Private (including infra+support) and show delta vs Hosted.

SLA: attaching a draft SLA and our latest SOC2 Type II report for Sarah’s review. The SLA draft includes 99.9% availability baseline and proposed remedies/credits for breach (negotiable by procurement/legal).

Proposed next steps:
- Marissa to run a 48–72 hour perf run using a small dedicated pool (we’ll need sample prompts / 100–200 representative requests). Can Finova provide a redacted prompt set + typical concurrency profile?
- Rishi to prepare a short perf run plan and expected metrics (p50/p95, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens) for the pilot.
- We’ll queue the SOC2 & SLA to Sarah and Janet; Marissa will be the primary for technical onboarding.
- Schedule 30-min sync Wed 04/21 09:00–09:30 PT (tentative) 1 please confirm.

Attaching: Redwood_SLA_Draft_v1.pdf, SOC2_TypeII_Report_2025.pdf

Hi Alyssa / team 1 quick technical notes to help with the perf plan: 

Measurement methodology: we’ll run the perf test against your redacted prompt set with traffic replay at representative concurrency. Key metrics: p50/p95 latency (end-to-end), tokens/sec, and cost per 1M tokens. We’ll include system-level traces so Sarah can validate resource isolation.

Deployment differences (short):
- Hosted API: fastest to start, fully managed, higher per-token cost, no VPC. Good for early evals.
- Dedicated Reserved: reserved GPU pools, predictable performance and cost, isolated within Redwood tenancy, supports reserved capacity pricing and private networking options. Good for pilot.
- Private/VPC: customer-managed network and control plane integration, required for regulated production. Performance comparable to Dedicated if comparable hardware is chosen.

Preliminary config recommendation for your sketch (short flows, <=256 tokens):
- Model: 7B–13B quantized depending on accuracy targets.
- Pool: 2–4 GPU nodes for the pilot (we’ll size after sample traffic).
- Batching: small micro-batches (to keep p50 low) with continuous batching to maximize throughput.

Estimated pilot outputs (very rough):
- p50: 120–300ms (depending on exact model & batching)
- p95: 400–800ms
- Cost: varies by model + quantization; we’ll produce a cost table for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private once we have prompt set.

Perf run plan: provide 100–200 redacted requests + target concurrency and we’ll run a 48-hour window; deliverable: latency percentiles, failure rates, token throughput, and a cost projection for 1M tokens.

I’ll draft the perf-run plan and send by EOD; Marissa will coordinate uploads/credentials for the prompt set.

Rishi
